actions.new_text: In Jos 5:4 and 1Ki 11:27 'the reason' introduces the explanation of why something was done: why Joshua circumcised the men, and why he lifted his hand against the king, the one who did it being named only in the verse before. The Hebrew word means a matter or account, here the matter that accounts for the deed.
actions.checked: Jos 5:4 (Joshua named) and 1Ki 11:27 (he lifted up his hand; no name in the verse)
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it named Jeroboam, whom 1Ki 11:27 does not name; the name is in the verse before

actions.new_text: The surface reason renders eighteen codes. As a word of the mind it is G3056 in 1Pe 3:15 (an account given) and H4486 in Dan 4:34 and Dan 4:36 (understanding restored), both nouns, and G2138 in Jam 3:17, an adjective (open to persuasion); as a verb it is H3198 in Isa 1:18 (to argue a case together). Elsewhere it is part of a phrase of cause: H6440I in Gen 41:31, H5921A, H1697M, H3651C, G1223, G5124, G0156, G2596, G0302, G1352, G5484, G1519 and H1961, and H2600 in Job 1:9 for without cause.
actions.checked: the morph of G2138 in Jam 3:17 (A-NSF, an adjective) and of G3056 and H4486 (nouns)
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it called G2138 a noun of the mind; the morph shows an adjective

it read there in Act 18:19 as qualifying the reasoning; by the grammar it qualifies the leaving

actions.new_text: In Act 17:2, Act 17:17, Act 18:4 and Act 19:8 the verb of reasoning (G1256) is qualified by time and frequency: on three Sabbaths, every day, every Sabbath, for three months. In Act 18:19 there qualifies the leaving of the others, not the reasoning. The qualifiers tell when and how often Paul reasoned, not how.
actions.checked: Act 18:19: he left them there, but he himself went into the synagogue and reasoned
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it read there in Act 18:19 as qualifying the reasoning; by the grammar it qualifies the leaving
